newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian energy minister says quit over reform team.
newsitem.headline: Russian energy minister says quit over reform team.

text.p: Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said on Tuesday that he had resigned because he did not fit in with the Kremlin's new reformist team.

"I'm not a man who is part of the team of those two deputy prime ministers," he said during an energy conference, referring to new cabinet reformers Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, both of whom have the rank of first deputy prime minister.
"I am a man of business, and it is back to business that I will go."
Rodionov submitted his resignation last Friday. He declined to say which energy company he would join.

The Kremlin has not yet named a replacement for Rodionov, who said he had heard that Alexander Samusev, vice-president of Rosprom-YUKOS and a former deputy minister in the Fuel and Energy and Finance Ministries, would replace him. Rosprom is an industrial holding firm attached to Menatep, a main shareholder in YUKOS, Russia's second largest oil producer.
When asked about his potential successor, Rodionov said, "I have heard only Samusev's name."
Rodionov, appointed only last August, was a gas transport specialist in a subsidiary of gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and left almost no changes in the energy sector.
Nemtsov, whose brief includes restructuring the natural monopolies, including Gazprom and RAO UES national electricity company, has said the two monopolies will not be broken up.
